Sheprd 

 
 
 
 

 
 sheprd.org ·
 Releases ·
 App updates ·

 GUI scope & configuration ·
 Performance report ·
 Contributing ·
 Star history 
 

A native Rust/GPUI workspace for terminals and AI agents on macOS, Linux, and
Windows. Organize repositories, worktrees, tabs and splits; chat with agents,
review their changes, track pull requests and usage, and work across local,
SSH and cloud machines. Browser previews, automations, mods and phone remote
control connect those workflows in one app. The iPhone and iPad app is in a
TestFlight beta.

Sheprd supports both an existing Herdr daemon and
herdr-core terminals. Releases
bundle a pinned herdr-core, so a separate Herdr 1 installation is optional.
Herdr 1 supplies terminal cells; herdr-core supplies raw output that
 sheprd-terminal emulates for the native view. The daemons own terminal
processes, so closing Sheprd leaves sessions running.

 Unaffiliated project. Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by
 Herdr or herdr.dev.

 Gallery

These existing captures predate the Sheprd rename and may show earlier names
and artwork; they are not refreshed screenshots of the rebrand.

 
 
 
 Workspaces, worktrees, and agents in one sidebar. Each agent carries the daemon's status dot (idle, working, or waiting on you), and tabs and splits are painted natively from the daemon's cells. 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 Worktree popover. Right-click a workspace or worktree for a new worktree, fan out, rename, Teleport, checkpoints, close, or delete the checkout. Double-click one to rename it. 
 
 
 
 
 Teleport . Move a worktree to another host with its commits, uncommitted changes, tabs, splits, running programs, and agent sessions. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Review an agent's changes . Open Review Changes from a tab strip's + menu, click any line to leave a note like a pull request comment, then Send to agent . 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Side-by-side diffs and a collapsed sidebar. Switch the review to side by side, and fold the sidebar to a rail that keeps every workspace and agent one click away. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Browser tabs with annotations . An agent opens its page with sheprd browser open ; you pick elements or regions, write notes, and send them back to that agent. Listening ports such as :4173 appear under their workspace. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Sidebar layouts. Pick a density or a design of its own from View > Layout or Settings; the choice applies live. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Plan usage . The status bar shows the signed-in AI services closest to their limits; click one for the details. 
 
 
 
 
 CPU and memory per host. The status bar follows the selected host, and with several hosts each sidebar host row shows its own, read over SSH for remote machines. NVIDIA, AMD, and Apple GPUs and their video memory can be turned on for the status bar and, on a line of their own, the sidebar. 
 
 
 
 Native settings. Grouped, searchable pages for themes, sidebar, fonts, tabs, notifications, and integrations; every change applies live to the open windows, and hovering a theme previews it in the app. 
 
 
 
 Sidebar page. Pick the layout and selection marks, tune spacing with sliders, and give each host its own colour. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Light or dark, or both. Any theme, or a light and dark pair that follows the system appearance; status colours keep their contrast on either. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Star your favorites. Pin the themes you keep coming back to at the top of the Color Scheme picker; one click stars or unstars a theme, and the stars are saved with your settings. 
 
 
 
 
 Hundreds of themes, one search away. Built-ins and Ghostty themes in one list: arrow or hover through them to preview each live, and your starred themes lead every search. 
 
 
 

Also included: saved SSH hosts with file copies,
inline images,
clickable links,
code navigation that jumps to a
symbol, file, or printed path:line in your terminal editor,
file drops,
editor groups, and
system notifications,
sounds, and a
Dock badge (on Windows, a
taskbar badge) when an agent needs you.

 Install

Release builds include a pinned herdr-core for local terminals. If Herdr 1 is
not installed, Sheprd opens a herdr-core shell; no separate daemon installation
is required. It joins an existing core first, otherwise starts your own
 herdr-core or the bundled companion. Source builds need a usable herdr-core
binary for this path.

Once Sheprd finds that Herdr 1 is not installed, it keeps using herdr-core
without retrying Herdr 1 in the background. If you install Herdr 1 later,
use Reconnect to check for it.

If you already use Herdr 1, Sheprd connects to its sessions
and may start your installed herdr server when the target session is absent.
It does not upgrade or migrate your personal daemon or move existing Herdr 1
sessions to Herdr 2. Explicitly confirming session deletion stops that named
session first; closing or removing the GUI leaves daemon sessions and saved
configuration intact.

Then install the latest stable release:

 Platform Command 
 --- --- 
 macOS brew install sheprd-labs/tap/sheprd 
 Linux (APT, DNF, zypper or pacman) curl -fsSL \ sh 
 Windows (PowerShell) irm \ iex 
 iPhone and iPad (beta) Join on TestFlight: sheprd.org/testflight 

Details, manual downloads, and other methods follow. Coding agents can read
sheprd.org/llms.txt for the same steps.

install.title: Install
install.html:
Release builds include a pinned herdr-core for local terminals. If Herdr 1 is not installed, Sheprd opens a herdr-core shell; no separate daemon installation is required. It joins an existing core first, otherwise starts your own herdr-core or the bundled companion. Source builds need a usable herdr-core binary for this path.

Once Sheprd finds that Herdr 1 is not installed, it keeps using herdr-core without retrying Herdr 1 in the background. If you install Herdr 1 later, use Reconnect to check for it.

If you already use Herdr 1, Sheprd connects to its sessions and may start your installed herdr server when the target session is absent. It does not upgrade or migrate your personal daemon or move existing Herdr 1 sessions to Herdr 2. Explicitly confirming session deletion stops that named session first; closing or removing the GUI leaves daemon sessions and saved configuration intact.

Then install the latest stable release:

Platform Command
macOS brew install sheprd-labs/tap/sheprd
Linux (APT, DNF, zypper or pacman) curl -fsSL https://sheprd.org/install.sh | sh
Windows (PowerShell) irm https://sheprd.org/install.ps1 | iex
iPhone and iPad (beta) Join on TestFlight: sheprd.org/testflight

Details, manual downloads, and other methods follow. Coding agents can read sheprd.org/llms.txt for the same steps.

The rename retains existing settings, sign-ins and install identities. See rebranding and rollout for the compatibility inventory and external rollout tasks; changing these source links does not deploy the site or transfer the repository.

macOS with Homebrew

Requires Homebrew and macOS 14.2 Sonoma or newer, on Apple Silicon or Intel. The cask installs the signed, notarized universal app.

brew install sheprd-labs/tap/sheprd
open /Applications/Sheprd.app

brew install resolves casks directly, so --cask is not required. Use the full name: it taps sheprd-labs/tap and trusts the cask for you, which Homebrew requires for any non-official tap. brew install sheprd alone needs brew trust --cask sheprd-labs/tap/sheprd first.

The cask is published to the tap by the release workflow. Installs from the older penso/tap keep upgrading as herdr-gpui at Herdr.app, because every release publishes there too. A cask install updates itself through Homebrew: the in-app updater detects that Homebrew owns the bundle and runs brew upgrade --cask on its cask for you, so Homebrew's records stay correct. If its metadata is stale, the updater runs brew update and retries once. The update panel shows progress throughout. macOS .dmg, Linux packages, and Windows installers and .zips are also published on Releases.

Betas are published as GitHub prereleases before being promoted to stable. To try them, turn on Settings > General > Install beta releases ([updates] channel = "beta"); turning it off never downgrades. Betas never reach the Homebrew tap, so a Homebrew install updates in place while the setting is on, and Homebrew takes it back at its next upgrade.

Linux packages

Each release publishes x86_64 and ARM64 builds as a .deb, an .rpm, an Arch Linux package, and a plain tarball, all containing the same executable. They need glibc 2.39 or newer (Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 13, Fedora 40, current Arch, openSUSE Tumbleweed or Leap 16, or later). The install script picks the package for your architecture and package manager, checks it against the release's published SHA-256, and installs it with sudo:

curl -fsSL https://sheprd.org/install.sh | sh

Read it first at site/install.sh. To install by hand instead, download the file for your architecture from Releases, then:

sudo apt install ./Sheprd-VERSION-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.deb      # Debian, Ubuntu
sudo dnf install ./Sheprd-VERSION-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.rpm      # Fedora
sudo pacman -U Sheprd-VERSION-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.pkg.tar.zst  # Arch Linux
# openSUSE: the release RPM is unsigned, which zypper stops on without the flag
sudo zypper install --allow-unsigned-rpm ./Sheprd-VERSION-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.rpm

The internal package name remains herdr-gpui; packages provide the canonical sheprd command and a real /usr/bin/herdr-gpui compatibility executable. The package manager pulls in the runtime libraries, including the Vulkan loader; a Vulkan driver for your GPU must also be present. On laptops with two GPUs, install the driver for the GPU your display uses, not only the discrete one. Without it, Sheprd renders on the discrete GPU, which can go to sleep while the window is hidden, so the window stays blank for a second or more each time you return to its workspace. On Arch Linux, install vulkan-radeon for AMD or vulkan-intel for Intel. App Updates detects which package manager owns the installed executable, downloads the matching .deb, .rpm, or Arch package, verifies its signed release metadata and checksum, then installs it through APT, DNF, zypper, or pacman with a PolicyKit authentication prompt. An .rpm goes to DNF where the host has it and to zypper on openSUSE. The authorized helper verifies and installs a protected root-owned copy. Choose Restart after installation; daemon and terminal sessions stay running. This requires pkexec and your desktop's PolicyKit authentication agent. Older builds that report “Package-managed installations cannot self-update” need one manual package upgrade to gain this support. Before a release, CI installs each package on Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 13 and Fedora 42, and the x86_64 Arch package on Arch Linux, then checks that the executable finds every library. The ARM64 Arch package targets Arch Linux ARM and is not install-tested.

On NixOS, or anywhere with Nix, build from source with the repository's flake:

nix run github:sheprd-labs/sheprd
# or add it to a configuration: inputs.sheprd.url = "github:sheprd-labs/sheprd";
# then environment.systemPackages = [ inputs.sheprd.packages.${system}.default ];

The flake builds with the toolchain pinned in rust-toolchain.toml on x86_64 and ARM64 Linux, and Apple Silicon macOS (14.2 or newer). On macOS, nix build also creates result/Applications/Sheprd.app, including the pinned herdr-core and the native Bluetooth helper; launch it with open result/Applications/Sheprd.app. Linux users supply their own Herdr or herdr-core daemon. Nix builds never update themselves; upgrade through Nix.

Windows installers

In PowerShell, on x86_64 or ARM64:

irm https://sheprd.org/install.ps1 | iex

The script (site/install.ps1) downloads the zip for your architecture, checks its published SHA-256, installs sheprd.exe and sheprd-launcher.exe alongside the legacy herdr-gpui.exe and herdr-gpui-launcher.exe entry points under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Herdr UI, adds that directory to your user PATH, and creates a Sheprd Start menu shortcut that opens the launcher. Prefer a regular installer? Each release also has Sheprd-VERSION-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc-setup.exe and Sheprd-VERSION-aarch64-pc-windows-msvc-setup.exe, which install the same files to the same place for the current user, without administrator rights, and add an uninstaller under Settings > Apps. Either way, the app updates itself from Check for Updates: it downloads the new installer, checks it against the release's signed manifest and its Authenticode publisher, runs it silently, and reopens. See Windows for what works on the platform.

Both add Open in Sheprd to folders in File Explorer, and to the empty space inside one, for your user only. It runs sheprd open on the folder through the launcher, so no console window appears: the running app focuses the folder's workspace or starts one there, and the app is started first when it is not running. On Windows 11 the entry is under Show more options, because the compact menu only lists commands of packaged apps. To remove everything install.ps1 added, run it with -Uninstall:

& ([scriptblock]::Create((irm https://sheprd.org/install.ps1))) -Uninstall

Uninstalling the regular installer from Settings > Apps removes the entry too.

From source

Install Rust/rustup and, on macOS, the Xcode command-line tools. The repository pins Rust 1.99.0 and GPUI 0.3.10 (the gpui-pre snapshot crate); the Rust version is declared in rust-toolchain.toml and mirrored in mise.toml, so mise install also provisions it.

git clone https://github.com/sheprd-labs/sheprd.git
cd sheprd
just run
